title: Windows XP Startup
blurb: Four seconds of pure early-2000s optimism, composed by Bill Brown and heard by more human beings than most symphonies will ever manage. The XP chime meant the family computer had finished thinking, the desktop with the green hill was loading, and the phone line was about to be occupied for an hour. It is genuinely well made — a rising figure that resolves rather than just stopping — which is why it aged into nostalgia instead of embarrassment. One of the most emotionally loaded sounds in computing, for a system that mostly ran Solitaire.
origin: The boot chime from Microsoft Windows XP (2001).
